A memo by Climate Power shared with several Democrat political organizations and 2028 presidential hopefuls states that "public opinion on data centers is cratering" and argues it provides a political opening on energy costs and environmental concerns, Axios reported Tuesday.
The "topline message" is that "Trump and Republicans have given AI data centers a blank check to raise our utility bills, poison our air, and drain our water," the memo stated.

Climate Power cited results from surveys by the Democrat-aligned polling firm Global Strategy Group. GSG conducted two surveys, each with a base sample of 1,000 registered voters nationwide, in April and June.

Climate Power said the polling showed that "data centers have gone from a relatively neutral issue to a growing political liability, with voters increasingly believing they drive up electricity demand, utility bills, and pressure on the grid."

The memo said Democrats can draw a contrast with Trump's AI and data center advocacy by uniting around three principles: requiring tech companies to pay their own way; powering data centers with clean energy; and giving communities a "real say" while ensuring they are informed about water and energy use.

Last month, Trump announced an expansion of his administration's Ratepayer Protection Pledge, aimed at ensuring the growth of data centers "powering America's AI dominance" does not raise electricity bills for households and businesses. Under the pledge, large data center operators commit to funding the electricity generation and infrastructure their projects require rather than passing those costs to ratepayers.
